items.title: A Concerning Amount of GTA Fans Would Give Up Their Pets to Play GTA 6 Early
items.excerpt: A poll of 1,300 American gamers shows some concerning trends regarding GTA 6 — more specifically, their willingness to abandon their pets for a chance at playing the game ahead of its release.
items.content_text: A poll of 1,300 American gamers shows some concerning trends regarding GTA 6 — more specifically, their willingness to abandon their pets for a chance at playing the game ahead of its release. GTA 6 might be the biggest pop culture phenomenon in human history. It’s certainly one of the most expensive video games ever made with a marketing budget to match, considering that Rockstar has literally taken over Miami with oodles of Vice City branding, alongside a collaboration with the Miami Heat . Before GTA 6’s big debut on Netflix , fans were literally camping outside of Rockstar’s headquarters, using special equipment to monitor oxygen levels , sound volume, and even count cars going in and out of the building for just a sliver of information about the highly-anticipated title. With just a few more weeks until launch, fans are more amped than ever to play the game — and some would even give up pretty important things if they had the chance to experience it before everyone else. A new survey by Unwind Media polled 1,347 American gamers to see how they felt about GTA 6. And while there were more than a few surprising responses, one stood out from the rest; according to the survey, 7% of polled fans said they would literally give up their pet for a month if they got to play the game a week early. Out of these fans, those who already pre-ordered the game were more likely to give up certain things. The number of deadbeat pet parents doubled within this group, with 13% of players who pre-ordered GTA 6 saying they would be willing to give up their pet to play it early. Other surprising admissions from the survey found that 21% of all fans polled would willingly give up intimacy to play GTA 6 a week early, meaning that one in five fans would make the trade. Of those fans, 25% were female, as opposed to 19% of male players. However, more heartwarmingly, over half of all participants said they planned to play the game together with their partner. A whopping 53% of those polled answered that this would be a good activity to play with their partner in crime; and funnily enough, more women than men were keen on doing this. 71% of gals are absolutely down to rob virtual corner stores with their boo, compared to 39% of dudes. This is good news, especially after a trend swept across social media that saw some concerned partners claiming the game’s relationship mechanic was technically “cheating.” According to the survey, just 8% of those surveyed genuinely felt this way — but we’ll just have to see how things pan out once the game is actually in players’ hands. GTA 6 releases on November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, and Xbox X|S.
items.title_en: A Concerning Amount of GTA Fans Would Give Up Their Pets to Play GTA 6 Early

items.title: John Goodman Says Digger Reviews 'Killed' the Movie Before It Was Released
items.excerpt: John Goodman believes the critical reception to Digger "killed" the movie before it had even been released.
items.content_text: John Goodman believes the critical reception to Digger "killed" the movie before it had even been released. Tom Cruise's latest film, Digger, is one of the biggest Hollywood bombs of 2026 . So far, the film has only made $49 million on a reported budget between $125–180 million, meaning it won't come close to breaking even in its theatrical run and probably won't make up the difference on home video. Given Cruise is seen as one of the last true movie stars, it was a pretty devastating blow. Cruise's Digger co-star, John Goodman, spoke about the situation with Josh Horowitz and believed that critics pushed anyone away from seeing it. Digger's Rotten Tomatoes score sits at 53%, making it one of Cruise's most divisive movies and the lowest-rated film in his filmography since 2017's The Mummy. "It hurt. They kinda killed us before we opened [with headlines like], 'This will only make $5," said Goodman. "And it [felt like] a good reason for people to avoid it. I'm proud of it. I had a ball doing it." Goodman went on to state that he believed in the message of Digger and defended the film, despite it not being universally loved. IGN gave Digger a 6 out of 10 , noting that the movie lacks the bite needed to sell its message, but has great performances and humor. "Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs," reads an excerpt from our review. "If you're an AMC A-List member (or have another cinema subscription), Digger is worth catching on the big screen." Maybe Digger will be one of those movies that ages well and fans will feel was misjudged. However, it may be years before it gets any kind of meaningful reevaluation. Whether this will deter Cruise from doing more big swings also remains to be seen, but at least the team behind the film stands by it.
items.title_en: John Goodman Says Digger Reviews 'Killed' the Movie Before It Was Released

items.title: Johnny Depp Is Open to Playing Jack Sparrow Again in a New Pirates of the Caribbean Movie
items.excerpt: Johnny Depp is open to playing Jack Sparrow again in a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie, despite saying he'd never work with Disney on the franchise ever again.
items.content_text: Johnny Depp is open to playing Jack Sparrow again in a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie, despite saying he'd never work with Disney on the franchise ever again. In a recent interview with Entertainment Tonight , Depp was asked if he had any interest in playing Sparrow again. He noted that he wanted to send the franchise off on a better note, presumably referring to the last film being a critical disappointment. "If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they're going to top off the Pirates [story]. The only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note. I'll go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything. If it's Jerry, I trust him. We have a deep friendship." Depp had previously stated during his legal battle with Amber Heard that he wouldn't work with Disney on a new Pirates movie , not even for $300 million and a million alpaca. It seems he's softened his stance on the matter, which has reportedly been the case for a while. Producer Jerry Bruckheimer has stated a few times over the last couple of years that he was having conversations with Depp about a new Pirates movie , but nothing has been locked in place. There is, however, a screenplay in the works , and the producer hopes to get a deal signed with Depp. This is the first time Depp has publicly revealed he's open to the idea since swearing off the idea in 2023. Disney had also been exploring a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie with Margot Robbie in the lead role, but that has yet to make any kind of notable progress. Depp hasn't been in many blockbuster roles since his legal battle with Heard, and he was notably forced to step down from his role in the Fantastic Beasts films due to his libel case against UK outlet The Sun. He was replaced by actor Mads Mikkelsen for the third film in the franchise, which also happened to be the last. Deep is now set to star in a new take on A Christmas Carol with the film Ebenezer , which releases on November 13. Whether Jack Sparrow will set sail again remains to be seen, but he does appear to be more into the idea than he was before.
items.title_en: Johnny Depp Is Open to Playing Jack Sparrow Again in a New Pirates of the Caribbean Movie

items.title: The Rings of Power Season 3 Co-Showrunner Confirms Harfoots Will Return
items.excerpt: Contrary to earlier reports, the Harfoots are still a part of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Season 3 albeit not to the degree they were featured in the Prime Video show’s first two seasons.
items.content_text: Contrary to earlier reports , the Harfoots are still a part of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power , Season 3 albeit not to the degree they were featured in the Prime Video show’s first two seasons. “[We] have not written out the Harfoots [from Season 3]”, co-showrunner Patrick McKay recently informed me at the show’s press junket. “I would say for myself and J.D. [Payne], my co-show runner, every season is its own opportunity and its own challenge. With Season 3, we really wanted to level up our game as dramatists. We really wanted to focus the show. We wanted to be more psychological, more emotional, wanted to do a darker season,” McKay explained. “It's the season where Sauron forges the One Ring , and we wanted that to unify every single storyline. We didn't want it to have sprawl the way we enjoyed having in the past. No, no. This was a time we wanted it to be one journey and on rails.” McKay continued: “That meant that if a story wasn't about the rings and wasn't about Sauron and wasn't about the One Ring, that to put it in there would feel forced and it wouldn't do justice to those characters. But don't worry, you can't count a halfling out, the Harfoots and Markella [Kavenagh] and Megan [Richardson]'s characters. They'll be back maybe sooner than you think.” How exactly the Harfoots will factor into the overall plot to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring – and just how much they will actually appear in Season 3 – remains to be seen. The last time we saw the Harfoots at the end of Season 2 , Nori Brandyfoot (Kavenagh) and her bestie Poppy Proudfellow (Richardson) bid farewell to the Stranger (Daniel Weyman). The two duo joined the Stoors as they left looking to find a new home after the Dark Wizard (Ciaran Hinds) destroyed their canyon. By the end of the Season 2 finale , the Stranger is dubbed “Grand Elf” by the Stoors, and thus the name Gandalf is born. The Rings of Power, Season 3 picks the story up five years later and chronicles the war to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring and binding its peoples to his will. The season introduces new characters, including an enigmatic “Orc with an Arc” who may or may not be an ally to the Elves. The first four episodes of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Season 3 will premiere on November 11, 2026. Episodes 305 & 306 will be available to stream on November 18, while the final two episodes of the season will be released on November 25.
items.title_en: The Rings of Power Season 3 Co-Showrunner Confirms Harfoots Will Return

items.title: Project Hail Mary Author Andy Weir Explains How He Would Fix the Star Wars Franchise
items.excerpt: Andy Weir, famous for penning The Martian and Project Hail Mary, has some strong ideas about how he would tackle telling stories in the Star Wars universe if he had the chance.
items.content_text: Andy Weir, famous for penning The Martian and Project Hail Mary , has some strong ideas about how he would tackle telling stories in the Star Wars universe if he had the chance. Andy Weir is well-versed in writing sci-fi stories with mass appeal. He is the author of two major novels in the genre, after all, both of which have been given the Hollywood treatment with big-budget film adaptations. And while his own tales have captivated audiences for over a decade, he has a good idea of what he’d do if he got put in charge of some pre-existing source material. In a November 2 interview with SlashFilm , Weirs was asked what he’d do if he were in charge of the Star Wars franchise — and he had a decisive answer. According to Weirs, moving away from the Galactic Civil War isn’t something that most fans are likely to get excited about; thus, in his opinion, a return to that time period focusing on different characters is the way to go. "Star Wars is more about massive upheaval. One problem that happens is, if you're going to have a story about a monumental war, then when it's over and the good guys win, you want it to stay that way. So it's very unsatisfying if you roll into a new monumental war,” he began. “I feel like the best way, in my opinion, to do another Star Wars movie — and I'm not George Lucas and this might be a terrible idea — would be to have the story of other people during the Galactic Civil War. “Think of it like this: We know what happened in World War II, but there are some really good fictional stories that take place during World War II. So if you treat the Galactic Civil War as, 'Okay, that's established canon, those are the things that happened,' but there's still a lot of stories to tell about other people living through those wars. So that's what I would do." To this point, Weirs had nothing but praise for Andor, Disney’s Star Wars series that takes place just before the Galactic Civil war with a focus on several different characters and their roles in the rebellion. However, he doesn’t feel like its sprawling story is something that could be translated to the big screen for a two-hour viewing experience. "Andor was amazing and really good, and it was a series and [that was the correct choice]. You're going to do a movie, you've got to tell your whole story in like two hours. So it needs to have a lot more — 'Andor' was very intellectual, extremely clever, extraordinarily well-written, very well — I mean, I loved everything about it. But it's not something that you could make into a movie,” he said. This is the latest big news to come from Weirs following his comments on AI , which are pretty bleak. Also speaking with SlashFilm, Weir admitted that it’s “only a matter of time” before the technology proliferates in careers like his, saying he “might be among the last generation of fully human writers."
items.title_en: Project Hail Mary Author Andy Weir Explains How He Would Fix the Star Wars Franchise

items.title: Black Friday 2026 Sale Dates and What to Expect
items.content_text: Black Friday is the biggest sales event of the year for every major retailer. It's also generally the best time to buy just about anything at a discount if you're trying to save money. With the majority of these sales taking place online these days, finding deals is easier than ever. But finding good deals has become increasingly difficult without a little help. If you're hoping to plan ahead for Black Friday this year, the IGN Finds team has you covered with everything you need to know to make smart shopping decisions in 2026. You can find all of our most recent deals coverage on our Black Friday hub or scroll down for more info about what to expect this month. Black Friday Sale Dates Black Friday always takes place on the day after Thanksgiving, which is November 27 this year. Of course, Black Friday sales don't really start on that Friday anymore. There are already early discounts happening across major retailers right now, but for a quick look at when the official Black Friday sales begin we've got an up-to-date list below: Amazon Black Friday - TBD Best Buy Black Friday - November 19 Walmart Black Friday - November 23 Target Black Friday - November 27 Costco Black Friday - November 27 When do early deals start? Best Buy, Target, Walmart, and Costco have all already announced early Black Friday sales with different start times. Target will be the first to drop a true early Black Friday sale from November 5-7, followed by Best Buy with a November 6 start date. What Deals Should You Expect? Just because every major retailer will have a Black Friday sale doesn't mean everything will be on sale this year. That being said, there are a few key categories you can absolutely expect to see good deals on in 2026. The first, and most obvious thing, is 4K TVs. Black Friday is, and will always be, the best time to buy a new TV at a low price. This same logic carries over to things like computer monitors and projectors. "AirPods, iPads, and Apple Watches will pretty much always go on sale for their lowest prices. The other Black Friday staple you can expect is Apple products. If you're hoping to grab the latest tech within the iOS ecosystem, November is absolutely the time to do so. AirPods , iPads , and Apple Watches will pretty much always go on sale for their lowest prices. All of the major retailers tend to compete to drop the latest AirPods models to a lower price than their competitors to drum up more online business. If you're in the market for toy deals, November is a great time to find discounts on less popular items and franchises. It's one of the best times of the year to buy LEGO, for example, but the majority of popular new sets for 2026 aren't going to get discounts. What you will find is major retailers dropping prices on older toys and LEGO sets that are up for retirement at the end of the year. Similar to toy deals, other physical media is sure to go on sale, but the selection will likely vary wildly. You can likely expect sites like Amazon to start dropping book deals early in the month ahead of the bigger sales. The same goes for 4K Blu-rays , board games , and vinyl records that tend to get swept up in various BOGO sales at Amazon and Target. You can also expect deals on physical video games for Nintendo , Xbox , and PS5 to drop a bit before Black Friday as well. What Probably Won't Go on Sale? Black Friday may be the best time to find deals, but that doesn't mean that every single product is going to get a discount. We're also in a unique position where economic factors have actually increased the price of some items to new highs, making it impossible to tell if something is a deal or just a bit of price normalization disguised as savings. So with that in mind, let's dive into some of the products you probably won't find a good discount on this year. Video Game Consoles If you've been following gaming news in 2026, things are looking pretty grim. We've already seen price increases on the Switch 2, Xbox, and PS5 and it's only getting worse. Xbox has even gone as far as to recommend that folks start trading in their unused consoles to help with the shortage. So yeah, it's pretty unlikely that we'll see any sort of console deal this year—especially with GTA 6 coming out right before Black Friday. The one exception to this is likely going to be Nintendo Switch 2 bundles . While these aren't exactly a great deal, they do tend to help you save at least some money on games and accessories. The best time to buy a Switch 2 was before the price increase, but the second best time is Black Friday. Gaming PCs, GPUs, and RAM PC gaming is having a difficult year and its all thanks to the influx of AI usage across the world. GPU prices have gone through the roof and the RAM shortage is likely only going to get worse in the years to come. All of this means that buying a gaming PC or gaming laptop has become more expensive than ever. If you want a high-end gaming rig at a decent price, you're pretty much out of luck. That doesn't mean there won't be any discounts available this year, but those discounts aren't going to be nearly as good as what we saw two years ago for the same products. It's pretty much now or never if you want to buy a gaming PC, but good luck finding anything good for under $1,500 this year. 4K Blu-ray Players With physical media experiencing a resurgence this year, it's become surprisingly hard to find a 4K Blu-ray player anywhere. The IGN Finds team noticed earlier this year that prices for the players were skyrocketing, if you could even find them in stock anywhere. So while Black Friday is a great time to buy 4K Blu-rays at a discount, you absolutely aren't going to find a way to play them for cheap. items.title: Pedro Pascal Is Hiding an Avengers: Doomsday Easter Egg on His Doctor Doom Halloween Costume, Fans Say
items.excerpt: Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal's Avengers: Doomsday Halloween costumes may have been more than just a fun treat for Marvel fans.
items.content_text: Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal's Avengers: Doomsday Halloween costumes may have been more than just a fun treat for Marvel fans. As footage of the two Marvel Cinematic Universe stars was shared across social media feeds throughout the spooky holiday weekend, die-hard fans began combing through every little detail to see if the Doctor Doom or Reed Richards actors had subtly teased any Easter Eggs. With less than 20 seconds of footage to look through, you'd think that wouldn't be the case, but you might want to think again. While Downey nearly recreated Mister Fantastic's blue retro-themed getup to a tee, Pascal's Doctor Doom costume looks a bit…lazier, at least at first glance. It seemed to be just a neat mask and cape paired with jeans and a sweatshirt, but upon closer inspection, it's what's on that sweatshirt that matters. In fact, it may tell us more about how deep Reed Richards and Victor von Doom's relationship goes. Zoom in on the MIT shirt and take a look at its logo. The low quality of Downey Jr.'s original upload makes it a bit hard to see all the details, but there's just enough here to suggest that we're looking at an illustration featuring both Doctor Doom and Mister Fantastic. So, why does this matter? Well, The Fantastic Four: First Steps did little to flesh out Reed and Victor's relationship ahead of Avengers: Doomsday. All we've really seen when it comes to the mask-wearing villain's ties to Marvel's first family thus far is a short clip of what looked like him spending some time with Franklin Richards . Reed and Victor are often known to have more than a few connections before, but outside of some trailer teases , it's hard to say just how close they ever were or still may be. MCU enjoyers believe this little logo is our first hint that Reed and Victor might go way, way back, with some fans theorizing that Pascal and Downey are teasing a bit of backstory that we might learn more about when the next Avengers movie premieres next month. +6 points for them telling us Reed and Victor went to MIT together by having them as the seal for the MIT logo. https://t.co/6yLLzOj4qH — Shaane (@bussdownhendrix) November 1, 2026 Others, however, aren't so convinced. As many have pointed out, the rough image quality might have everyone looking a little too deeply into what's on Pascal's Doom costume. While some doubters still appreciate the callout, they suspect we could just be getting a sneak peek at some new merch. As with most early fan theories for big-budget comic book movies, these theories could totally pan out, or they could mean nothing. It's hard not to try and read too much into any potential Easter Eggs or teases when Avengers: Doomsday is only a little more than one month away. Fans again pulled out magnifying glasses when a father's day post shared by Downey suggested the upcoming MCU movie might dive into Doctor Doom's backstory . At the very least, we know all will be revealed when the movie premieres December 18.
items.title_en: Pedro Pascal Is Hiding an Avengers: Doomsday Easter Egg on His Doctor Doom Halloween Costume, Fans Say

items.title: Terminally Ill GTA 6 Fan Dies 3 Weeks Before Game's Launch, Fans Pay Their Respects
items.excerpt: A terminally ill GTA 6 fan has died three weeks before the game's launch.
items.content_text: A terminally ill GTA 6 fan has died three weeks before the game's launch. Back in August, a man named Jerry, known online as Void Only, made a viral TikTok video revealing that he had been hospitalized due to an interstitial lung disease and was in need of a lung transplant. However, he noted that his unique situation meant that his lungs were attached to his chest wall, and any surgery would be bloody and dangerous. In that same post, he noted that he just wanted to play GTA 6, and poked fun at Rockstar's many delays for the game. In the comments, fellow players rallied around him and were rooting for him to keep going until the release of GTA 6. A GoFundMe was set up to pay for his transplant and other needs, with supporters donating $50,000 in a matter of days . In September, Jerry got his transplant, but various complications eventually caused him to lose function of his body. Jerry's sister confirmed via his socials that he died over the weekend, but was extremely appreciative of all of the people who tried to help and support him. The news comes just three weeks before GTA 6's release, which Jerry had planned to stream with his community once it was released. In the comments of his sister's post, fans expressed sadness over Jerry not being able to make it to the release of the game he'd been excitedly waiting so long to play. "I was really rooting for him. I'm sorry for your loss," said one commenter. "I'm adding Void to my gamertag in his honor when GTA releases," said another. This tragic outcome has left supporters devastated. Jerry himself stayed optimistic in his final months and kept a positive attitude, prompting fans to echo his enthusiasm. Jerry's sister also noted that his mother is planning to do a balloon release in his honor, and more details will be shared at a later date.
items.title_en: Terminally Ill GTA 6 Fan Dies 3 Weeks Before Game's Launch, Fans Pay Their Respects

items.title: Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show Dubbed the 'Most International Yet' with Almost 220,000 Attendees
items.excerpt: Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show Dubbed the 'Most International Yet' with Almost 220,000 Attendees
items.content_text: Organisers have dubbed this year’s Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show as the “most international edition in the show’s history,” with an estimated 219,546 attendees from 113 countries descending on the event last week in Bangkok. The four-day show was headlined by a keynote address from legendary gamemaker and Doom co-creator John Romero, who presented a panel called ‘Why We Still Make Games’, recounting the achievements, failures, and lessons learnt across his five decades in the industry. Other notable panels were hosted by members of Adhoc Studio, the makers of the breakout 2025 narrative game Dispatch, and Bloober Team CEO Piotr Babieno, who delved into the slowburn success story of his studio’s horror hit, Cronos: The New Dawn. Out on the showfloor fans were able to enjoy 470 titles from indies and major gaming brands like Capcom, Bandai Namco Entertainment, SEGA, and Ubisoft. A number of these included hotly anticipated titles like Final Fantasy VII Revelation, Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, Stranger Than Heaven, and Total War: Warhammer 40,000. Debuting at this year’s event was the pop culture festival, ACE (Anima Asia Comics Content Entertainment Expo), and America’s Got Talent 2026 winner, Nene Royal, performed the event’s theme song during the opening ceremony. The Thailand Game Awards, which also ran during the show, named Capcom’s Pragmata as its Game of the Year. “This was the most international show we’ve ever staged,” said Mathias Kuepper, managing director and regional president, APAC, Koelnmesse. “Exhibitors from 29 countries and regions came to Bangkok to sign deals, not only to show games. That tells the global industry that Southeast Asia is no longer a market to watch. It’s a market to be in, and this is where deals get done.” It has been confirmed by the organisers that Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show will return to Bangkok from 21 to 24 October 2027.
items.title_en: Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show Dubbed the 'Most International Yet' with Almost 220,000 Attendees

Professional grade controllers generally command a premium price point, and SCUF is no exception, with its top-end controllers priced upwards of $200. Save 10% Off the Ultimate PlayStation 5 Controller The officially licensed SCUF Omega PlayStation 5 controller is, frankly, what the DualSense Edge should have been. It adopts the DualSense's familiar layout with dual analog sticks and iconic geometric face buttons, but just about every component has been upgraded. For starters, both analog sticks are equipped with SCUF's Endurance TMR sensors. TMR joysticks are a step up from Hall Effect. As if that still wasn't enough inputs, five "G-Keys" are positioned along the bottom edge of the controller, with two of the keys being programmable via the SCUF mobile app. Note that this controller is also compatible with PC. items.title: Blackpink's Jisoo Confirms She Referenced Resident Evil's Ada Wong in New Music Video
items.excerpt: Blackpink’s Jisoo has confirmed that she referenced Resident Evil’s Ada Wong in the music video for her solo song Addicted.
items.content_text: Blackpink’s Jisoo has confirmed that she referenced Resident Evil’s Ada Wong in the music video for her solo song, Addicted. The song debuted over Halloween weekend, with its accompanying music video showing Jisoo wearing a variety of different looks. One of these outfits, however, struck a chord with certain members of her fanbase due to how startlingly similar it looked to a character from Resident Evil . At the beginning of the music video, Jisoo wears a black bob and a red bodycon-style dress — a look that’s basically synonymous with Ada Wong, who almost always wears some variation of this style in each game she appears in. Fans couldn’t help but notice the similarities and asked the K-pop star if this was intentional on her very own app. “Red outfit + short hair look is totally Ada Wong from Resident Evil,” one wrote. Surprisingly, Jisoo confirmed that this was actually intentional. "I love Biohazard (Resident Evil) sooo much, so I wanted to copy it,” she said in a reply. Jisoo is open about her love for Resident Evil; she spoke about the series on Hot Ones earlier this year, saying she was “addicted” to the games. “It’s fast-paced,” she explained. “Something will suddenly pop out at you, so you have to be quick and process it all and take care of the situation. That’s why it’s able to hold my attention, and time just flies right by.” Funnily enough, Jisoo isn’t the only K-pop star to draw comparisons with Ada Wong recently; in August, Babymonster’s Asa received similar comments from fans after she posted photos of herself on social media wearing a black bob and a red dress , sparking a cute portmanteau of ‘Asa Wong’ from her fanbase. While Asa hasn’t yet responded to these remarks, Jisoo is an unabashed fan of the games, to the point where she made sure Ada was somehow represented in her latest song. In other Resident Evil news, Zach Cregger, who directed the series’ most recent movie adaptation, said he would still like to be involved in some way if a sequel gets made, though not as a director. Thus far, it’s unclear whether or not another Resi movie is in the works, but given that Capcom has doubled down on its plans to continue expanding its IP with merch, new content, and movies, it’s possible that we get another look at Raccoon City — especially given how successful the first film was at the box office .

items.title: ‘Those Are the Wrong Reasons to Make a Movie’ — Godzilla Minus Zero Director Takashi Yamazaki on Setting Aside the Urge to One-Up Godzilla Minus One
items.excerpt: Godzilla Minus Zero writer, director, and VFX supervisor Takashi Yamazaki says that getting caught up in besting Godzilla Minus One "risked diluting what makes the movie great in the first place."
items.content_text: How does a filmmaker attempt to follow up a history-making movie with an even bigger and better sequel? For Godzilla Minus One and Zero writer, director, and VFX supervisor Takashi Yamazaki, that line of thinking doesn’t even belong in the equation. “In the beginning I thought, ‘Well, how do I outdo its predecessor and how do we make a movie that's going to win all these awards and it's going to be bigger in scale?’” Yamazaki told IGN during an interview near Godzilla Minus Zero’s debut at the New York Film Festival. “But I think it's very dangerous to create a movie with that type of mindset because you're going to risk diluting what makes the movie great in the first place. So those are the wrong reasons to make a movie and it ends up becoming an antagonist in your moviemaking process.” Godzilla Minus One was released in 2023 and quickly caught fire. Yamazaki’s take on a post-WWII Godzilla was especially praised for its human-focused story and highly impressive VFX, done with a famously lean team of 35 artists . It went on to beat Hideaki Anno’s 2016 Shin Godzilla at the box office, becoming the highest-grossing Godzilla movie to date . At the 2024 Oscars, where the cast and crew walked the red carpet holding Godzilla figurines and wearing very cool Godzilla shoes, the film took home the trophy for Best Visual Effects. The win was historic on many levels: It was the first Japanese film to claim the award, minted the first Gen Z winner in the category , and did so with the smallest budget of any other category in more than a decade . (Reports had put the cost between $10–15 million.) “Godzilla Minus One was loved and so well received by so many around the world and received a lot of awards, which I think was unthinkable when we first set out and went to make it,” Yamazaki said. “So thinking about a sequel, of course, there's gonna be a certain amount of pressure.” Godzilla Minus Zero is due out in the U.S. this week — it opened in Japan on November 3 for Godzilla Day — and the anticipation is high following its film festival premieres this fall that have been universally rapturous. Naturally, it’s a bigger film in just about every way. First and foremost, it’s got an extra kaiju (which means, a new pair of shoes to go with it). It’s both the first R-rated Godzilla movie and the first Japanese film to be specifically shot for IMAX screens. At a panel at New York Comic-Con, the aforementioned Gen Z Oscar winner, VFX artist and compositor Tatsuji Nojima, gave an example of just how much more intensive the effects process becomes with that extra screen space: The shot of Godzilla leaping out of the ocean behind a seaplane from the first trailer was made entirely using VFX that required rendering 2 billion particles, versus the 200 million particles needed for an ocean sequence in Godzilla Minus One. (Nojima also shared that the scene was made by just two people: himself and an animator.) Though the exact figures are unknown, Yamazaki has confirmed that the budget was certainly bigger this time around. It’s projected to rake in $25–35 million its opening weekend, according to Box Office Pro , which would more than double Godzilla Minus One’s first weekend earnings of $11.4 million. Still, for Yamazaki, the important part of making a successful sequel was in rejecting the anxiety of feeling like he needed to one-up Godzilla Minus One at all. “I think when I decided not to think about it was a huge sense of relief for me and just simply focus on making a movie entertaining, making something fun, making something that has a message,” he said. “The moment where I felt like, yes, I did it was probably when I shed off all that extra pressure and thought, ‘You know what? I'm just going to make a fun movie.’ [That] was my own tipping point.” Godzilla Minus Zero opens in the U.S. on Friday, November 6. We said it “ups the ante on the carnage, providing plenty of satisfying and visually amazing scenes of giant-monster destruction” in our review . Photo credit: Jerritt Clark/Getty Images

items.title: Sony Wants to Buy Your PS5 Console for $400
items.excerpt: Sony is offering $400 to people who are willing to part ways with their PS5 and two controllers.
items.content_text: Sony is offering $400 to people who are willing to part ways with their PS5 and two controllers. As spotted by ResetEra user Jay_Horror , PlayStation is sending out notifications to fans who have the PlayStation app on their phones. The notification tells users that they can trade in their console to Sony and have money sent directly to their bank account. This offer is valued up to $400 for anyone who has a standard PS5 and two controllers. Although trade-in programs, particularly around the holiday season, aren't uncommon for retailers like GameStop, it isn't as normal to see platform holders reaching out directly to customers like this. It may suggest that Sony is preparing for a shortage of hardware or is interested in pre-owned stock that it can sell at a more affordable price than a brand-new unit. PlayStation 5 consoles are currently $600 - $650, depending on whether you get a disc drive. If you want the more premium PS5 Pro console, it will set you back $900. However, due to the demand for the Pro in the lead-up to GTA 6's release, it has been hard to get one at retail price. As a result, resellers and even retailers like GameStop are selling used PS5 Pros for as much as $1,400 . If you're someone who bought a PS5 before prices began to jump and don't use it, this isn't a terrible deal. Given the console initially cost $500, getting $400 back (so long as you also acquired an additional controller at some point) is a solid trade-in value. At this point in the PS4's life cycle, you wouldn't have gotten anywhere near close to $400 back at a retailer like GameStop.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Added Fast Travel Before Devs Decided It Never Needed It in the First Place
items.excerpt: The Legend of Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma asked the Ocarina of Time remake team to add fast travel warp points throughout Hyrule, but it didn't take long for him to realize that was probably a bad idea.
items.content_text: The Legend of Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma asked the Ocarina of Time remake team to add fast travel warp points throughout Hyrule, but it didn't take long for him to realize that was probably a bad idea. Aonuma, one of the franchise's most experienced developers, touched on the trashed concept as part of an Ask the Developer interview shared by Nintendo today. The Nintendo Switch 2 version of one of the most influential video games of all time already seems to have made a few changes to its gameplay formula, but there's one change that he said was better left on the cutting room floor. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time players and speedrunners have spent who knows how much time making Link forward roll to quickly cross great distances. When looking back at how the series has evolved with entries like Breath of the Wild, Aonuma said he found room for improvement, pointing to the wide-open (and iconic) Hyrule Field as one location that might benefit from a fast-travel option. It sounds like it didn't take too long to realize that maybe Nintendo got it right the first time around, though. "So I asked the team to add warp points that didn’t exist in the original game, giving players access to shortcuts," he explained. "But when we actually tried playing the game with those warp points, we realized that we were missing out on the moments of discovery that came from stopping along the way and wondering, 'Wait, what’s this?' "Through this development process, we were reminded once again just how important those moments are to the very structure of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. So even though I was the one who proposed adding warp points, they just weren't working for me in the end, so I got the team to take them all back out again. (Laughs)" That's not to say Nintendo didn't find room to experiment with the structure of Link's first real 3D adventure. Although, for example, the development team intentionally chose to keep loading screens to preserve the feeling of entering a new area, we already know that Link will be able to move faster thanks to a sprint feature. Players can also now take advantage of a dedicated jump button. What might sound like negligible adjustments to some might be earth-shaking changes for others, but we'll have to wait to see just how different The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2 is from the original. "Looking at what they ultimately created, I’m impressed by how rich an experience they were able to craft from a game that first came out 28 years ago," Aonuma added. "At the beginning of development, I remember thinking, 'They could be making more changes.' But as the project went on, it really came across just how deeply this development team cared about the original game, far more than we had imagined." IGN gathered a list of 40 changes we noticed after getting a better look at the remake in September. We then took a closer look with a preview of our own . If you're wondering why Nintendo opted to make an Ocarina of Time remake in the first place, you can click here . The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5. Google is celebrating the release with a time-travling Easter Egg .

items.title: A Buggy World of Warcraft Mount Has Renewed Player Frustrations at the State of Retail
items.excerpt: While World of Warcraft Forever is heading to what is likely a monumental release on November 4, some retail World of Warcraft players have been feeling neglected, and a recent mount has become a flashpoint for that frustration.
items.content_text: While World of Warcraft Forever is heading to what is likely a monumental release on November 4, some retail World of Warcraft players have been angry at the state of the game, and a recent mount has become a flashpoint for that frustration. Blizzard released the 'Hot Motocross Bunmover 4000' mount as part of its November Trading Post, and it's just a cute little tricycle with an oven attached to the back to tie in with Thanksgiving. The problem, though, is that its wheels aren't animated. They also clip through the ground, making it look like it's just sliding around on the floor. In the grand scheme of things, this would have been a minor blip, but the mount has ignited player frustrations that have been simmering for the last year since Midnight released. Back when Midnight launched, everything seemed great, and it reviewed well. Here at IGN, we gave it a 9, with reviewer Len Hafer saying, "Enthralling zones and a satisfying endgame loop carry World of Warcraft: Midnight from high point to high point." But just like any MMO, the real test is the updates that follow release. Those updates have been marked by rapid-fire content with 'invasions' that feel like they've been copied and pasted from previous seasons and lackluster writing, culminating in the current patch, which kills off a beloved Horde character pretty much out of the blue. So, when Blizzard released the Hot Motocross Bunmover 4000, it took all of that frustration and gave it a confectionary symbol. Reddit user iamShorteh posted a screenshot of the mount on Reddit , captioned, "Attached: image of the mount, this is how the wheels remain permanently on the Hot Motocross Bunmover 4000. Literally unplayable." Then, user audioshaman replied, "But Holly Langdale assured me that the 8 week patch cadence has had zero impact on quality." That was followed by user gladfanatic saying, "They straight up don’t care anymore in retail lol." That eight-week patch cadence started back in Dragonflight as a way to eliminate the long content droughts that the MMO had in past expansions. While it was fine for a while, that schedule has grown problematic over the last couple of expansions, with bugs and repeated content plaguing nearly every patch. It's little wonder, then, why WoW Forever developers told me last week that the Classic+ mode would be opting for a slower update schedule . But there are some WoW fans that think the problems run deeper than WoW's update schedule. User Jocic posted, "Genuinely, what is happening? At this point, you can't even use the eight-week cadence as an excuse for them. How is EVERYTHING broken?" Even on Twitter, Windows Central Executive Editor Jez Corden retweeted a video of the mount , saying, "Blizz has really phoned it in with World of Warcraft: Retail." However, while people are frustrated with the state of retail, World of Warcraft has been through harder times. The game has survived the lows of Warlords of Draenor and Shadowlands, even when Classic launched right before the latter. Retail WoW will probably live on through these current quality issues, but hopefully the backlash will at least get Blizzard to at least consider changing up the speed at which it's pumping out new content. It's time to pull the ripcord. At least in the interim, WoW Forever is on the eve of its full release. Despite the problems with its name reservation system last week, it's shaping up to be a massive game. Even in the beta, WoW Forever devs were shocked at how many people were playing , and once the floodgates open on Wednesday, those numbers are only going to go up.

items.title: Zach Cregger Says He Still Wants to 'Have a Hand' in Future Resident Evil Sequels
items.excerpt: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger says that he’d still want to “have a hand” in potential sequels for his hit horror adaptation, despite swearing off future “franchise” films.
items.content_text: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger says that he’d still want to "have a hand" in potential sequels for his hit horror adaptation, despite swearing off future "franchise" films. Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation was a hit at the box office , but its reception was starkly different among hardcore fans of the original games. Rather than attempting to retell stories players have already experienced, he opted for a different approach by following an average Joe as he navigates the chaos of the Raccoon City Incident — and this rubbed a vocal portion of the fanbase the wrong way. As a result, Cregger has adamantly decided against ever working on a "franchise" again , a word he used on an episode of The Town with Matthew Belloni . "If there were five Resident Evil movies that you just produced but didn’t write or direct, would you be okay with that, or not?" the host asked him. "I would want to have some hand in them," Cregger answered. "I can’t help but have an idea for where that franchise — I’m calling it a franchise — could go. So, certainly." This isn’t the first time Cregger has mentioned his vision for a sequel to his Resident Evil movie; he spoke about the possibility with The Playlist in September, saying he "can’t help thinking about other places this story could go." "With Barbarian, I’ve never entertained the idea of a sequel or another movie in that universe because that story is, at its heart, so foul," he continued. "What makes Barbarian interesting is the unfolding of the narrative, not the subject matter. I don’t think I want to write another story about what that movie is about. But this is different. I want to talk about the ending of this movie so badly, because there is a big aspect of it that’s worth discussing. This is a different situation." As previously mentioned, however, the idea of remaining with the Resident Evil franchise — at least as far as films are concerned — has put a sour taste in his mouth due to fans' reactions to his take on Capcom's flagship horror franchise. In this same interview, Cregger bemoaned the discourse that surrounded the movie, saying that fans weren’t actually focused on the film itself but instead how well it matched up with the games . "I think I was frustrated at the conversation around Resident Evil and how much of the conversation really didn't have anything to do with the movie," he said. “It had everything to do with whether the movie was living up to the different standards that different fans of the games had. Whether it was using the characters or not, or what did I get wrong in the lore? It was just a lot about, 'Why isn't this like the source material, or why is it good that it's not like the source material?' All the conversation just felt like it was about not the movie." Speaking with IGN , Cregger admitted he was "naive" to think that fans would be gung-ho about his take on the source material; though, despite it all, it seems like he’d still want to be attached to future adaptations of Resident Evil in some shape or form.

items.title: The Avatar: Seven Havens Season 1 Blu-ray and Steelbook Is Up for Preorder at Amazon
items.content_text: The first season of Avatar: Seven Havens has officially wrapped up . Unsurprisingly, it quickly became one of the most popular shows on Paramount+, which has now decided to honor the ATLA tradition of physical media releases. The first official Blu-ray set for Avatar Seven Havens is now available to preorder for $39.99 at Amazon. A steelbook will also be available for $48.99 , but Amazon hasn't revealed any imagery of the more expensive edition. Amazon also hasn't confirmed a release date for either listing. Where to Preorder Avatar: Seven Havens Blu-ray Other than the preliminary artwork, there aren't many details available about the Blu-ray or the Steelbook just yet. According to the Amazon listing, the total runtime for the Blu-ray is 4 hours and 59 minutes, which lines up with how long it takes to watch all of the episodes on Paramount+. This would indicate that the physical release doesn't include any bonus features, but it's too early to confirm whether that's the case. Avatar: Seven Havens premiered on October 9 and wrapped up its final batch of episodes on October 30, so it's not too surprising that the Blu-ray preorder went up pretty quickly as well. The Avatar franchise has a history of releasing physical discs at the end of each season. While it wasn't 100% clear if Seven Havens would follow suit now that the IP is under the Paramount banner, the most recent film, Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender, got the 4K Blu-ray treatment after streaming on Paramount+. What we said about the season 1 finale "Seven Havens ends its first season going for the heart with a powerful quartet of episodes which go very, very dark and answer some big questions while raising others. It’s safe to say after 13 episodes, Seven Havens is a worthy successor to both The Last Airbender and Legend of Korra. Bring on Book 2." Read IGN's full review . When will we get season 2? We already know that Seven Havens has been renewed for four total seasons , but we don't know when the next batch of new episodes will actually drop. Paramount+ hasn't announced any sort of official release date for season 2, though rumors have been swirling online about a potential November 2026 drop. As for what to expect next season., IGN had the chance to talk to the showrunners about some of our burning questions now that season 1 has wrapped up. Without getting into too many spoilers, the final episode had a pretty dramatic conclusion that will almost certainly shift the dynamic in the upcoming season.
